title: The Workshop Pods
briefing: Two GPU teams are fighting. The render team's old code only works with rgbglow 0.9, but the test team needs the new rgbglow 1.3. With only one Python install, somebody loses. Unless... every team gets its own sealed workshop pod: a virtual environment!
hints: venv.create("name") gives you back an environment. env.install("pkg==version") installs into THAT environment only.

venv.activate("gpu-tester") switches to that environment, so import rgbglow now gets ITS version. rgbglow.__version__ tells you which one you have. env.freeze() gives that environment's requirements text.

render = venv.create("gpu-render") / render.install("rgbglow==0.9") / render.install("boardcheck==2.1") / tester = venv.create("gpu-tester") / tester.install("rgbglow==1.3") / venv.activate("gpu-tester") / import rgbglow / tester_version = rgbglow.__version__ / then for env in [render, tester]: open(f"{env.name}-requirements.txt", "w") and write env.freeze()
bonus: Activate gpu-render, then import rgbglow again with importlib.reload or a fresh import. Which version do you get now?
